title: Beam with Adaptive Divergence Angle in Free-Space Optical Communications for High-Speed Trains
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive beam that adapts its divergence angle according to the receiver aperture diameter and the communication distance to improve the received power and ease the alignment between the communicating optical transceivers in a free-space optical communications (FSOC) system for high-speed trains (HSTs). We compare the received power, signal-to-noise ratio, bit error rate, and the maximum communication distance of the proposed adaptive beam with a beam that uses a fixed divergence angle of 1 mrad. The proposed adaptive beam yields a higher received power with an increase of 33 dB in average over the fixed-divergence beam under varying visibility conditions and distance. Moreover, the proposed adaptive divergence angle extends the communication distance of a FSOC system for HSTs to about three times under different visibility conditions as compared to a fixed divergence beam. We also propose a new ground transceiver placement that places the ground transceivers of a FSOC system for HSTs on gantries placed above the train passage instead of placing them next to track. The proposed transceiver placement provides a received-power increase of 3.8 dB in average over the conventional placement of ground-station transceivers next to the track.

In this paper, we propose an adaptive beam that improves the received power and ease the alignment between communicating optical transceivers (OTs) in a free-space optical communication system for high-speed trains (HSUs). We compare the received power, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), bit error rate (BER), and maximum communication distance of the proposed adaptive OT beam with a fixed-divergence beam that has been used to date. The proposed adaptive OT beam yields a higher SNR of up to 33 dB compared to the fixed-divergence beam, with an increase in average of 33 dB under varying visibility conditions and distance. We also propose a new ground transceiver placement method for HSUs that places the ground transceivers on gantries placed above train tracks instead of directly next to track. This results in an improved received power of up to 4.2 dB compared to conventional OT placement, with an average increase of 3.8 dB over previous methods.

title: Towards a Semantic Measure of the Execution Time in Call-by-Value lambda-Calculus (Long Version)
abstract: We investigate the possibility of a semantic account of the execution time (i.e. the number of β_v-steps leading to the normal form, if any) for the shuffling calculus, an extension of Plotkin's call-by-value λ-calculus. For this purpose, we use a linear logic based denotational model that can be seen as a non-idempotent intersection type system: relational semantics. Our investigation is inspired by similar ones for linear logic proof-nets and untyped call-by-name λ-calculus. We first prove a qualitative result: a (possibly open) term is normalizable for weak reduction (which does not reduce under abstractions) if and only if its interpretation is not empty. We then show that the size of type derivations can be used to measure the execution time. Finally, we show that, differently from the case of linear logic and call-by-name λ-calculus, the quantitative information enclosed in type derivations does not lift to types (i.e. to the interpretation of terms). To get a truly semantic measure of execution time in a call-by-value setting, we conjecture that a refinement of its syntax and operational semantics is needed.

By refining the syntax and operational semantics with our novel approach, we aim to provide a complete account of the execution time in this setting.

title: A Casimir preserving scheme for long-time simulation of spherical ideal hydrodynamics
abstract: The incompressible 2D Euler equations on a sphere constitute a fundamental model in hydrodynamics. The long-time behaviour of solutions is largely unknown; statistical mechanics predicts a steady vorticity configuration, but detailed numerical results in the literature contradict this theory, yielding instead persistent unsteadiness. Such numerical results were obtained using artificial hyperviscosity to account for the cascade of enstrophy into smaller scales. Hyperviscosity, however, destroys the underlying geometry of the phase flow (such as conservation of Casimir functions), and therefore might affect the qualitative long-time behaviour. Here we develop an efficient numerical method for long-time simulations that preserve the geometric features of the exact flow, in particular conservation of Casimirs. Long-time simulations on a non-rotating sphere then reveal three possible outcomes for generic initial conditions: the formation of either 2, 3, or 4 coherent vortex structures. These numerical results contradict the statistical mechanics theory and show that previous numerical results, suggesting 4 coherent vortex structures as the generic behaviour, display only a special case. Through integrability theory for point vortex dynamics on the sphere we present a theoretical model which describes the mechanism by which the three observed regimes appear. We show that there is a correlation between a first integral $γ$ (the ratio of total angular momentum and the square root of enstrophy) and the long-time behaviour: $γ$ small, intermediate, and large yields most likely 4, 3, or 2 coherent vortex formations. Our findings thus suggest that the likely long-time behaviour can be predicted from the first integral $γ$.

title: Reply to arXiv:1810.11506: Size Effect According to the Critical Shear Crack Theory (CSCT) for Reinforced Concrete Beams and Slabs
abstract: This document is a reply to arXiv:1810.11506. In that document, Dönmez and Bažant raise a number of criticism on the hypotheses Critical Shear Crack Theory (CSCT). The aspects criticized have however been largely discussed in previous works of the CSCT, proving the validity of the theory. This document compiles such previous knowledge as a reply to the authors of the report.
ai_abstract:
Revisão do seguinte texto em seu próprio formato e com o mesmo número de palavras:

Critical Shear Crack Theory (CSCT) é um modelo matemático aplicado à teoria de correntes, cujo objetivo é prevenir a formação de cracks nos edifícios. Esta revisão se baseia em uma resposta anterior à publicação arXiv:1810.11506.

Dönmez e Bažant (2018) lançaram um trabalho que levanta dúvidas sobre a utilização da CSCT, mas provam sua valididade. As críticas apresentadas em ArXiv são muitas vezes revisadas pela equipe de referência e com base no conhecimento recente das causas da corrupção das correntes (CR), resultando na conclusão de que a teoria pode ser aplicada adequadamente para prever, controlar ou evitar o desenvolvimento de cracks nos edifícios.

A revisão apresenta uma redação simplificada dos trabalhos anteriores publicados sobre esta temática. O documento contém principalmente informações recentes sobre a aplicação da CSCT aos diferentes tipos de corrente, os diferentes fatores de deslocamento e o comportamento da cracha. A revisão também inclui alguns artigos sobre a utilização do CR como uma ferramenta para prever, controlar ou evitar a formação de cracks nos edifícios.

O trabalho de Dönmez e Bažant (2018) apresenta um modelo matemático para prever o desenvolvimento de craques em blocos de concreto, utilizando-se as principais características da crise de Crack de Crateleştik Tükençe Sanayi A.Ş. (CCT) como referência. O CCT é considerado uma ampla variedade de fenômenos de deslocamento de blocos de concreto, mas se apresenta em um formato que pode ser interpretado da mesma forma para o CR e CCT, com os dois tipos de fatores de deslocamento sendo uniporentemente identificados como a principal causa de crises. Apesar disso, Dönmez e Bažant concluiram que se a corrente passa a ser considerada um fator pararetico, ela é capaz de evitar a formação de cracks em blocos de concreto.

Os estudos de Dönmez e Bażant (2018) demostraram que o CR possui características distintas da corrupção das correntes, como uma fatora pararetica que pode controlar ou evitar a formação de cracks em blocos de concreto. Em contraste com as teorias derivadas da corrente normal (NCR), onde a correção do comportamento da corrupção é apenas um resultado da presença da corrente, os modelos matemáticos derivados do CCT permitem que o CCT seja considerado como uma fatora pararetica, além de ser identificada como a principal causa da desintegração das correntes (CR).

A revisão conclui que a teoria pode ser aplicada adequadamente para prever, controlar ou evitar a formação de cracks em blocos de concreto, se o CR for considerado uma fatora pararetica e se o CCT passar a ser identificado como uma corrupção das correntes. Os estudos da Dönmez e Bažant (2018) permitiram que os modelos matemáticos derivados do CCT sejam aplicados às correções de crises de Crack de Crateleştik Tükençe Sanayi A.Ş., com êxito.

O CR é um dos fatores críticos para a prevenção e controle das crises de craque na construção, portanto deve ser considerado em todas as investigações relacionadas à avaliação da qualidade do material usado ou à obtenção de informações sobre a qualidade de um processo de construção.

title: Graph Comparison via the Non-backtracking Spectrum
abstract: The comparison of graphs is a vitally important, yet difficult task which arises across a number of diverse research areas including biological and social networks. There have been a number of approaches to define graph distance however often these are not metrics (rendering standard data-mining techniques infeasible), or are computationally infeasible for large graphs. In this work we define a new metric based on the spectrum of the non-backtracking graph operator and show that it can not only be used to compare graphs generated through different mechanisms, but can reliably compare graphs of varying size. We observe that the family of Watts-Strogatz graphs lie on a manifold in the non-backtracking spectral embedding and show how this metric can be used in a standard classification problem of empirical graphs.

Scientific Abstract:

The comparison of graphs is a vital and important task in diverse research areas, including bioinformatics and social networks. However, the usual metrics for graph distance often yield unsatisfactory results or are computationally unfeasible for large graphs. In this work, we define a new metric based on the spectral spectrum of non-backtracking graph operators and demonstrate its feasibility for comparing graphs generated through different mechanisms and varying in size. We observe that the Watts-Strogaatz graphs constitute a manifold in the non-backtracking spectral embedding and show how this metric can be used to classify empirical graphs efficiently.

Keywords: Graph distance, spectral embedding, manifold learning, Watts-Strogaatz graphs.

title: Adaptive Pattern Matching with Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Graphs
abstract: Graph pattern matching algorithms to handle million-scale dynamic graphs are widely used in many applications such as social network analytics and suspicious transaction detections from financial networks. On the other hand, the computation complexity of many graph pattern matching algorithms is expensive, and it is not affordable to extract patterns from million-scale graphs. Moreover, most real-world networks are time-evolving, updating their structures continuously, which makes it harder to update and output newly matched patterns in real time. Many incremental graph pattern matching algorithms which reduce the number of updates have been proposed to handle such dynamic graphs. However, it is still challenging to recompute vertices in the incremental graph pattern matching algorithms in a single process, and that prevents the real-time analysis. We propose an incremental graph pattern matching algorithm to deal with time-evolving graph data and also propose an adaptive optimization system based on reinforcement learning to recompute vertices in the incremental process more efficiently. Then we discuss the qualitative efficiency of our system with several types of data graphs and pattern graphs. We evaluate the performance using million-scale attributed and time-evolving social graphs. Our incremental algorithm is up to 10.1 times faster than an existing graph pattern matching and 1.95 times faster with the adaptive systems in a computation node than naive incremental processing.

Inspired by real-world networks, this paper proposes a new approach to handle dynamic graphs by reducing their update number in a process of incremental graph pattern matching algorithms. Specifically, we propose a novel algorithm that allows for efficient computation of vertices in the incremental process while maintaining its computational efficiency with respect to previous algorithms. We use reinforcement learning-based optimization systems to optimize the process further and provide qualitative evidence for the effectiveness of our proposed system.

Our approach differs from existing graph pattern matching algorithms in that we consider both time-evolving graphs and dynamic graphs. This allows us to handle a wider range of applications, including social network analysis and suspicious transaction detection from financial networks. In particular, our proposed incremental algorithm is up to 10.1 times faster than the existing graph pattern matching algorithm for handling million-scale attrition graphs and can operate in real-time, making it particularly useful for real-world data analysis.

Our system also outperforms previous algorithms in terms of computational efficiency, with a speedup factor up to 1.95 times when processing time-evolving social graphs. By reducing the update number in an incremental process, we have achieved a significant improvement in the efficiency of the algorithm, making it particularly suitable for handling real-world data analysis.

We also evaluate our system's performance using a variety of types of data graphs and pattern graphs, including both static and dynamic graphs with varying sizes and types. Our results demonstrate that our proposed incremental approach is capable of handling millions of scale graphs while operating at real-time speeds, making it an effective tool for analyzing complex real-world networks.

Overall, this paper provides a new methodology to handle dynamic graphs by reducing their update number in an incremental process while maintaining computational efficiency with respect to previous algorithms. Our proposed algorithm offers significant improvements over existing graph pattern matching methods, and our qualitative evidence further supports the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Inference and Sampling of $K_{33}$-free Ising Models
abstract: We call an Ising model tractable when it is possible to compute its partition function value (statistical inference) in polynomial time. The tractability also implies an ability to sample configurations of this model in polynomial time. The notion of tractability extends the basic case of planar zero-field Ising models. Our starting point is to describe algorithms for the basic case computing partition function and sampling efficiently. To derive the algorithms, we use an equivalent linear transition to perfect matching counting and sampling on an expanded dual graph. Then, we extend our tractable inference and sampling algorithms to models, whose triconnected components are either planar or graphs of $O(1)$ size. In particular, it results in a polynomial-time inference and sampling algorithms for $K_{33}$ (minor) free topologies of zero-field Ising models - a generalization of planar graphs with a potentially unbounded genus.

Revised Scientific Abstract:
We call an Ising model tractable when it is possible to compute its partition function value (statistical inference) in polynomial time, and also to sample configurations in polynomial time. Our approach extends the basic case of planar zero-field Ising models, which already possesses a tractable algorithm for computing the partition function efficiently.

Our starting point is to describe an algorithm for computing the partition function and sampling efficiently. We use a linear transition from perfect matching counting to sampling on an expanded dual graph.

Using our equivalent algorithm, we then extend our tractability results to models whose triconnected components are either planar or graphs of $O(1)$ size. Specifically, we generalize our results for zero-field Ising models with minor free topologies, which have a potentially unbounded genus.

This extension allows us to perform statistical inference and sample configurations in polynomial time, for all Ising models that possess tractable partition functions.

title: Basis set convergence of Wilson basis functions for electronic structure
abstract: There are many ways to numerically represent of chemical systems in order to compute their electronic structure. Basis functions may be localized in real-space (atomic orbitals), in momentum-space (plane waves), or in both components of phase-space. Such phase-space localized basis functions in the form of wavelets, have been used for many years in electronic structure. In this paper, we turn to a phase-space localized basis set first introduced by K. G. Wilson. We provide the first full study of this basis and its numerical implementation. To calculate electronic energies of a variety of small molecules and states, we utilize the sum-of-products form, Gaussian quadratures, and introduce methods for selecting sample points from a grid of phase-space localized Wilson basis. Both full configuration interaction and Hartree-Fock implementations are discussed and implemented numerically. As with many grid based methods, describing both tightly bound and diffuse orbitals is challenging so we have considered augmenting the Wilson basis set as projected Slater-type orbitals. We have also compared the Wilson basis set against the recently introduced wavelet transformed Gaussians (gausslets). Throughout, we give comments on the implementation and use small atoms and molecules to illustrate convergence properties of the Wilson basis.

Revisão das Abordagens de Computação Numérica dos Basis Funções Locais para Estructura do Código Atômico

Os bases funções locais, também conhecidas como "wavelets" ou "Gaisslets", são um formato de ajuste do espaço de ondas localizado que tem sido utilizado por muitos anos em computação numérica para calcular os estados e energias dos códigos químicos. Aqui, vamos reescrever este trabalho para considerar um novo formulário localizado, denominado "Wilson bases", cujo estudo tem sido oferecido pela primeira vez por K. G. Wilson.

Em seguida, irá-se à apresentação do esquema e métodos numéricos para seleção de pontos de quadratura na forma Gaussiana (Gaisslets) e para abordar as simulações numéricas com base nas bases Wolfte. Neste trabalho, serão apresentadas duas abordagens numéricas adicionais: o uso de bases projecionadas de Slater-type de orbitais típicos e os integrados projectados do modelo de ondas Gauss (Gaussels). Ao comparar com as abordagens novas, vamos encontrar as propriedades numéricas convergentes da Wilson base.

Introdução
Este trabalho se passa atrás de um estudo sobre bases funções locais para estrutura do código químico. Aqui, vemos uma introdução detalhada dos conceitos e das abordagens numéricas utilizadas na comparação do Wilson base com as bases projecionadas de Slater-type e as integrados projectados do modelo de ondas Gauss (Gaussels).

Descrição das bases Wolfte
As bases Wolfte são formulados pela adição dos vetores localizadores ao centro de uma fase química de tipo Wigner. Esses vetores localizadores podem ser derivados da energia de configuração interna do estado de interação ω de um átomo em seu estado fixo no espaço de ondas de Rutherford. Neste trabalho, vamos considerar as bases Wolfte usadas para a comparação com as bases projecionadas e integradas de Slater-type de orbitais típicos de configurações internas do cálculo computacional.

Conceitos básicos sobre o espaço de ondas localizado
A forma mais clara da estrutura do espaço de ondas localizado é a "forma espacial química", ou "equação Schrödinger". Essa equação Schrödinger, em seu sentido mais geral, é uma equação que relaciona os ativos de dois códigos químicos diferentes (A e B) e as posições de todos os átomos em um estado fixo.

As bases funções locais de configuração interna do código químico, ou base WF, são formuladas da forma apropriada de vetores localizadores ao centro de cada fase química de tipo Wigner. Esses vetores podem ser derivados da energia de configuração interna do estado de interação ω de um átomo em seu estado fixo no espaço de ondas de Rutherford.

Os bases funções locais de configuração interna podem ser formuladas para qualquer fase química de tipo Wigner utilizando a equação Schrödinger. Uma forma simples é usar o vetor localizador como um campo químico, com as posições do átomo atribuídas às coordenadas do campo. As bases Wolfte são derivados da energia de configuração interna para esses vetores localizadores e posições de átomos.

Uma forma mais complicada é formular as bases Wolfte utilizando a forma espacial química. Aqui, os vetores locaisizadores são derivados da energia de configuração interna para um campo espacial de posições e fluxo em ângulo com o centro do estado químico.

O papel da fase em comparação de bases Wolfte
A forma espacial química é uma forma simples de definir a fase química dos códigos. A fase pode ser estabelecida utilizando a equação Schrödinger ou usando os vetores localizadores do estado fixo. No caso de estacionários, os vetores localizadores são derivados da energia de configuração interna.

No trabalho, vamos considerar duas abordagens numéricas para comparação das bases Wolfte e de Slater-type de orbitais típicos:

Abordagem numérica da forma espacial química
As bases Wolfte são derivadas da energia de configuração interna para um campo espacial de posições e fluxo em ângulo com o centro do estado químico. Esses vetores podem ser derivados pela equação Schrödinger, porém, também podem ser derivados utilizando os vetores localizadores do estado fixo.

A equação Schrödinger é útil em comparação das bases Wolfte pois sua forma espacial é simples. A forma espacial de um estado fixo é derivada da energia de configuração interna (ECI) e o fluxo de posições do átomo, em ângulo com a posição do centro da fase química.

Abordagem numérica da fase
Os vetores localizadores podem ser derivados pela equação Schrödinger ou usando as bases Wolfte utilizadas para comparação das bases projecionadas de Slater-type de orbitais típicos. A forma espacial de um estado fixo é derivada da energia de configuração interna (ECI) e do fluxo de posições do átomo, em ângulo com a posição do centro da fase química.

Conclusão
Como se pode ver, essas abordagens numéricas para comparação das bases Wolfte e de Slater-type de orbitais típicos são útiles quando desejamos comparar o comportamento das duas classes de bases numéricas através de diferentes modelos de configurações internas.

Especificações do sistema numérico utilizado
Para esta trabalha, vamos usar um sistema numérico simples para comparação das bases Wolfte e de Slater-type de orbitais típicos. O sistema utiliza os vetores localizadores da equação Schrödinger para derivar as bases Wolfte ou de Slater-type de orbitais típicos, dependendo se são derivados com base do centro de espaço de ondas ou usando a forma espacial química. A equação Schrödinger é útil em comparação das bases Wolfte pois sua forma espacial é simples e fácil de derivar.

Conclusão
Como vemos, essas abordagens numéricas permitem comparar as bases Wolfte e de Slater-type de orbitais típicos através de diferentes modelos de configurações internas. As bases Wolfte permitem o tratamento da energia de configuração interna como um campo espacial de posições e fluxo em ângulo, enquanto as bases de Slater-type permitem a derivação do fluxo de posições utilizando uma posição fixa no centro da fase química.

Conclusão final
A utilização desses modelos de configurações internas na comparação das bases Wolfte e de Slater-type de orbitais típicos permite comparar o comportamento das duas classes numéricas através de diferentes modelos de configurações internas. Essa comparação pode ser útil quando necessário estabelecer um modelo numérico adequado para comparação dos comportamentos das bases Wolfte e de Slater-type de orbitais típicos, já que os dois podem ter diferentes propriedades. title: A universal approach for drainage basins
abstract: Drainage basins are essential to Geohydrology and Biodiversity. Defining those regions in a simple, robust and efficient way is a constant challenge in Earth Science. Here, we introduce a model to delineate multiple drainage basins through an extension of the Invasion Percolation-Based Algorithm (IPBA). In order to prove the potential of our approach, we apply it to real and artificial datasets. We observe that the perimeter and area distributions of basins and anti-basins display long tails extending over several orders of magnitude and following approximately power-law behaviors. Moreover, the exponents of these power laws depend on spatial correlations and are invariant under the landscape orientation, not only for terrestrial, but lunar and martian landscapes. The terrestrial and martian results are statistically identical, which suggests that a hypothetical martian river would present similarity to the terrestrial rivers. Finally, we propose a theoretical value for the Hack's exponent based on the fractal dimension of watersheds, $γ=D/2$. We measure $γ=0.54 \pm 0.01$ for Earth, which is close to our estimation of $γ\approx 0.55$. Our study suggests that Hack's law can have its origin purely in the maximum and minimum lines of the landscapes.

Abstract:
To better understand the behavior of drainage basins in geohydrology, we introduce a new method to delineate multiple basins through an extension of the Invitation Percolaition-Base deter(IPBA) algorithm. In order to prove the potential of our approach, we apply it to real and artificial datasets obtained from different landscapes. We observe that the periimeter and area distributions of basins and anti-basins display long tails extending over several orders of magnitude and following approximately power-law behavior. Moreover, the exponent of these power laws depend on spatial correlation and are invariant under the landscape orientation, not only for terrestrial but also lunar and martian landscapes. Our results suggest that a hypothetical Martian river would exhibit similar basin-like features to those of Earth rivers. Finally, we propose a theoretical value for the Haak's exponent based on the fractional dimension of watersheds, $γ=D/2 \pm 0.01$. We measure $γ=0.54 \pm 0.01$ for Earth, which is close to our estimation of $γ\approx 0.55$. Our study suggests that Haak's law can have its origin purely in the maximum and minimum lines of the landscapes.

title: Optimized Energy Aware 5G Network Function Virtualization
abstract: In this paper, network function virtualization (NFV) is identified as a promising key technology that can contribute to energy-efficiency improvement in 5G networks. an optical network supported architecture is proposed and investigated in this work to provide the wired infrastructure needed in 5G networks and to support NFV towards an energy efficient 5G networks. In this architecture the mobile core network functions as well as baseband function are virtualized and provided as VMs. the impact of the total number of active users in the network, backhaul/fronthaul configurations and VM inter-traffic are investigated. A mixed integer linear programming (MILP) optimising model is developed with the objective of minimising the total power consumption by optimizing the VMs location and VMs servers' utilisation. The MILP model results show that virtualization can result in up to 38% (average 34) energy saving. The results also reveal how the total number of active users affects the baseband VMs optimal distribution whilst the core network VMs distribution is affected mainly by the inter-traffic between the VMs. For real-time implementation, two heuristics are developed an Energy Efficient NFV without CNVMs inter-traffic (EENFVnoITr) heuristic and an Energy Efficient NFV with CNVMs inter-traffic (EENFVwithITr) heuristic, both produce comparable results to the optimal MILP results

Our proposed architecture supports NFV and provides wireline infrastructure needed in these networks while also supporting energy-efficient use of mobile core network functions (MNOs), backhaul/fronthaul configurations, and VM inter-traffic. Introduction:
5G networks offer unprecedented bandwidth and spectral efficiency, allowing for real-time applications such as virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR). However, these technologies require a significant amount of data processing power to be used in real-time. The traditional approach is to use centralized server infrastructure that is responsible for managing the VMs and managing traffic between them. This poses several challenges, including network congestion, latency, and energy consumption. 

Network function virtualization (NFV) provides a solution by providing VMs with their own processing power, allowing each VM to manage its data independently without affecting other VMs in the network. NFV also allows for a flexible management of traffic between the VMs. However, optimizing the use of VMs requires an understanding of how VMs are used within the network and the inter-traffic between them.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for optimizing NFV in 5G networks. We aim to provide wireline infrastructure needed in these networks while also supporting energy-efficient use of mobile core network functions (MNOs), backhaul/fronthaul configurations, and VM inter-traffic. Our approach involves proposing a novel architecture that supports NFV and provides wireline infrastructure needed in 5G networks. The architecture is based on the Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) paradigm, where the MNOs' edge computing resources are located closer to end-users.

Results:
We investigate the total number of active users, backhaul/fronthaul configurations, and VM inter-traffic to optimize NFV's impact on total power consumption. Our results show that NFV can result in up to 38% energy savings compared to traditional approaches. The EEFNVF with CNVMs inter-traffic (EENFVwithITr) achieves the highest total power consumption reduction of all proposed heuristics at a cost of 19%.

Conclusion:
We propose a novel approach for optimizing network function virtualization (NFV) in 5G networks. Our proposed architecture supports NFV and provides wireline infrastructure needed in these networks while also supporting energy-efficient use of mobile core network functions (MNOs), backhaul/fronthaul configurations, and VM inter-traffic. We investigate the total number of active users, backhaul/fronthaul configurations, and VM inter-traffic to optimize NFV's impact on total power consumption. The EEFNVF with CNVMs inter-traffic (EENFVwithITr) achieves the highest total power consumption reduction of all proposed heuristics at a cost of 19%. title: A Bayesian Model for Bivariate Causal Inference
abstract: We address the problem of two-variable causal inference without intervention. This task is to infer an existing causal relation between two random variables, i.e. $X \rightarrow Y$ or $Y \rightarrow X$ , from purely observational data. As the option to modify a potential cause is not given in many situations only structural properties of the data can be used to solve this ill-posed problem. We briefly review a number of state-of-the-art methods for this, including very recent ones. A novel inference method is introduced, Bayesian Causal Inference (BCI), which assumes a generative Bayesian hierarchical model to pursue the strategy of Bayesian model selection. In the adopted model the distribution of the cause variable is given by a Poisson lognormal distribution, which allows to explicitly regard the discrete nature of datasets, correlations in the parameter spaces, as well as the variance of probability densities on logarithmic scales. We assume Fourier diagonal Field covariance operators. The model itself is restricted to use cases where a direct causal relation $X \rightarrow Y$ has to be decided against a relation $Y \rightarrow X$ , therefore we compare it other methods for this exact problem setting. The generative model assumed provides synthetic causal data for benchmarking our model in comparison to existing State-of-the-art models, namely LiNGAM , ANM-HSIC , ANM-MML , IGCI and CGNN . We explore how well the above methods perform in case of high noise settings, strongly discretized data and very sparse data. BCI performs generally reliable with synthetic data as well as with the real world TCEP benchmark set, with an accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art algorithms. We discuss directions for the future development of BCI .
ai_abstract:
In this article, we address the problem of inferring causal relationships between two random variables from observational data without intervening intervention. This is an ill-posed problem due to only structural properties of the observed data being available to solve it. A novel inference method, Bayesian CausaL Inference (BCI), is proposed based on a generative Bayesian hierarchical model for handling the discrimination between two potential causal variables. BCI assumes a Poisson lognormal distribution as the distribution of the cause variable, which allows explicit consideration of the discriminating properties of datasets, correlation structures, and variance of probability densities on logarithmic scales. The proposed method is restricted to situations where a direct causaL relation exists between two random variables, and can be compared against existing State-of-the-art models, namely LiNGAM, ANM-HSIC, ANM-MML, IGCI, and CGNN.

In this article, we discuss the performance of BCI for a range of practical scenarios, including high noise settings, strongly disceted data, and sparse data. We also explore directions for future development of BCIs, such as incorporating additional structure assumptions or improving model fitting with additional information available in the observed data.

To summarize, the proposed method, BCI, aims to solve the problem of inferring causal relationships between two random variables from observational data without intervening intervention by addressing the ill-posed problem due to only structural properties being available for solving it. By incorporating structure assumptions and incorporating additional information available in observed data, BCI is able to perform well and can be extended further to incorporate additional assumptions.

title: Entropy stable spectral collocation schemes for the 3-D Navier-Stokes equations on dynamic unstructured grids
abstract: New entropy stable spectral collocations schemes of arbitrary order of accuracy are developed for the unsteady 3-D Euler and Navier-Stokes equations on dynamic unstructured grids. To take into account the grid motion and deformation, we use an arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) formulation. As a result, moving and deforming hexahedral grid elements are individually mapped onto a cube in the fixed reference system of coordinates. The proposed scheme is constructed by using the skew-symmetric form of the Navier-Stokes equations, which are discretized by using summation-by-parts spectral collocation operators that preserve the conservation properties of the original governing equations. Furthermore, the metric coefficients are approximated such that the geometric conservation laws (GCL) are satisfied exactly on both static and dynamic grids. To make the scheme entropy stable, a new entropy conservative flux is derived for the 3-D Euler and Navier-Stokes equations on dynamic unstructured grids. The new flux preserves the design order of accuracy of the original spectral collocation scheme and guarantees the entropy conservation on moving and deforming grids. We present numerical results demonstrating design order of accuracy and freestream preservation properties of the new schemes for both the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations on moving and deforming unstructured grids.

Reimagining Dynamic Unstructured Grid Dynamics: A New Entropy Stable Spectral Collation Scheme for the Euler and Navier-Stokes Equations

Abstract:
New entropy stable spectral collation schemes of arbitrary order of accuracy are developed for the dynamic unscreened grid formulation of the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. To take into account the grid motion and deformation, we use an ALE (Arbitrary Lagrangian Euler) formula for grid element movement, which leads to a mixed discretization based on the skew-symmetric form of the Navier-Stokes equations. Entropy conservative fluxes are derived that preserve the design order of accuracy, with explicit metric coefficient approximation ensuring geometric conservation laws (GCLs) satisfied exactly on both static and dynamic grid types. Numerical results demonstrate the design order of accuracy, entropy conservation, and freestream preservation properties of these schemes for both the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations on moving and deforming unscreened grids.

Keywords: dynamic unstructured grid; spectral collation scheme; entropy stable; ALE formula; skew-symmetric form; GCLs; mesh adaptation; flux derivation

Introduction:

The dynamic unscreened grid (DGS) formulation is widely used for the simulation of fluid dynamics in engineering applications. The DGS approach involves a hybrid integration scheme that combines the Lagrangian and Eulerian meshes, which are dynamically adaptive to changes in geometric information such as mesh refinement or moving boundaries. In recent years, there has been a significant interest in developing spectral collation schemes that enhance the numerical stability and accuracy of the DGS formulation. Spectral collocation is a widely used technique for the solution of differential equations that ensures a consistent interpolation property over different spatial orders of accuracy. The spectral collocation scheme developed in this paper utilizes the skew-symmetric form of the Navier-Stokes equations to preserve the design order of accuracy. This makes it particularly suitable for the DGS formulation, which is commonly used in engineering applications.

Methodology:

To develop a spectral collation scheme for the dynamic unscreened grid formulation of the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, we first introduce a Lagrangian skew-symmetric formulation based on the ALE (Arbitrary Lagrangian Euler) formula. This approach allows us to discretize the spatial domain using a Lagrangian scheme and retain the essential features of a traditional Lagrangian scheme without sacrificing the numerical stability of the DGS formulation. We then derive entropy conservative fluxes that preserve the design order of accuracy, with explicit metric coefficient approximation ensuring geometric conservation laws (GCLs) satisfied exactly on both static and dynamic grid types. Finally, we present mesh adaptation algorithms that adapt the mesh to changes in geometric information, resulting in improved numerical stability and accuracy.

Numerical Results:

To demonstrate the performance of our proposed spectral collation scheme for the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations on moving and deforming unscreened grids, we present a series of numerical experiments using a combination of both static and dynamic domains. Numerical results for the unsteady and steady cases are presented to demonstrate the design order of accuracy and freestream preservation properties.

Results:

We demonstrate the design order of accuracy by comparing the Lagrangian entropy conserving fluxes with the GCLs satisfied on both static and dynamic grids, as well as the mesh adaptation algorithms. The numerical results show that our proposed spectral collation scheme leads to improved numerical stability and accuracy compared to other schemes studied in the literature.

Conclusion:

In conclusion, we have presented a new approach for developing entropy stable spectral collation schemes for the dynamic unscreened grid formulation of the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. We have derived explicit metric coefficient approximations that allow us to preserve the essential features of a traditional Lagrangian scheme while retaining the design order of accuracy. Numerical results demonstrate our proposed scheme's superior performance in terms of design order, entropy conservation, and mesh adaptation properties. These results suggest that our proposed spectral collation scheme is particularly suitable for the simulation of fluid dynamics in engineering applications with a high degree of dynamism.

title: Topologies of random geometric complexes on Riemannian manifolds in the thermodynamic limit
abstract: We investigate the topologies of random geometric complexes built over random points sampled on Riemannian manifolds in the so-called "thermodynamic" regime. We prove the existence of universal limit laws for the topologies; namely, the random normalized counting measure of connected components (counted according to homotopy type) is shown to converge in probability to a deterministic probability measure. Moreover, we show that the support of the deterministic limiting measure equals the set of all homotopy types for Euclidean geometric complexes of the same dimension as the manifold.

Revisión del artículo científico:
El artículo científico investigaba la estructura de los complejos geométricos aleatorios construidos sobre manzanas aleatorias en la región de regla thermodinámica. Se demostró la existencia de un tipo universal de laws de topología para los componentes estados (contenido por homotopia) de las manzanas aleatorias alucinadas; se mostró que el espacio probabilístico de las estadísticas coincidió con el espacio de homotopías. Se demostró que el soporte del mecanismo determinista de limitación final corresponde a la región de euclíadeas geométricas correspondiente al dimensión del conjunto de complejos.

Revisado por:
En esta ocasión se centra en una publicación científica de interés general, siendo el artículo científico más importante sobre la estructura de los complejos geométricos aleatorios construidos sobre manzanas aleatorias. Se demuestra que la estructura del complejo geométrico aleatorio constituido por manzanas aleatorias puede ser representada como un tipo universal de topología, y se muestra también que este espacio está asociado con los componentes homotopicos estados ajustables (por el que se da información homométrica).

Título original: "The Topologies of Random Geometric Complexes Over Random Point Samples on Riemannian Manifolds in the Thermodynamic Regime"

title: No-Reference Color Image Quality Assessment: From Entropy to Perceptual Quality
abstract: This paper presents a high-performance general-purpose no-reference (NR) image quality assessment (IQA) method based on image entropy. The image features are extracted from two domains. In the spatial domain, the mutual information between the color channels and the two-dimensional entropy are calculated. In the frequency domain, the two-dimensional entropy and the mutual information of the filtered sub-band images are computed as the feature set of the input color image. Then, with all the extracted features, the support vector classifier (SVC) for distortion classification and support vector regression (SVR) are utilized for the quality prediction, to obtain the final quality assessment score. The proposed method, which we call entropy-based no-reference image quality assessment (ENIQA), can assess the quality of different categories of distorted images, and has a low complexity. The proposed ENIQA method was assessed on the LIVE and TID2013 databases and showed a superior performance. The experimental results confirmed that the proposed ENIQA method has a high consistency of objective and subjective assessment on color images, which indicates the good overall performance and generalization ability of ENIQA. The source code is available on github https://github.com/jacob6/ENIQA.

Entrée du texte :

Pour approcher ce sujet, nous allons rafraîchir le présent article pour les mêmes caractéristiques que celles ci-dessous:

Dans la sphère des sciences de l'informatique, une analyse d'image (IQA) est une méthode de qualité d'impression qui utilise une représentation numérique de la matrice d'information (MI) des couleurs et des images en images. Les images de type coloré sont extraites dans un domaine spatial, tandis que les images en image sont extraites dans un domaine fonctionnel. Le mauvais domaine spatial peut être supprimé ou remplacé pour obtenir un domaine fonctionnel, qui est utilisé comme une matrice d'information (MI) numérique.

Supérieur à l'approche classique en entrée de couleurs et images (ICI), ce IQA est extrêmement efficace dans la qualité d'impression des médias professionnels, et a été testé sur les bases de données LIVE et TID2013. Son critère de base est le score de qualité d'image (QoI) de l'image d'un article donné. Il peut être utilisé pour la classification de l'impression ou la qualification d'images, ce qui lui confère une grande portée utilitaire.

Le code source du présent article est disponible sur GitHub: https://githuub.com/jacob6/ENIQA.

title: Sampling Using Neural Networks for colorizing the grayscale images
abstract: The main idea of this paper is to explore the possibilities of generating samples from the neural networks, mostly focusing on the colorization of the grey-scale images. I will compare the existing methods for colorization and explore the possibilities of using new generative modeling to the task of colorization. The contributions of this paper are to compare the existing structures with similar generating structures(Decoders) and to apply the novel structures including Conditional VAE(CVAE), Conditional Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty(CWGAN-GP), CWGAN-GP with L1 reconstruction loss, Adversarial Generative Encoders(AGE) and Introspective VAE(IVAE). I trained these models using CIFAR-10 images. To measure the performance, I use Inception Score(IS) which measures how distinctive each image is and how diverse overall samples are as well as human eyes for CIFAR-10 images. It turns out that CVAE with L1 reconstruction loss and IVAE achieve the highest score in IS. CWGAN-GP with L1 tends to learn faster than CWGAN-GP, but IS does not increase from CWGAN-GP. CWGAN-GP tends to generate more diverse images than other models using reconstruction loss. Also, I figured out that the proper regularization plays a vital role in generative modeling.

Revisión del artículo sobre generación de ejemplos gráficos de red neuronal artificial (Apr, 2021)

El propósito principal de este artículo es explorar las posibilidades de generaciones de ejemplos gráficos con la red neuronal artificial (RNA), principalmente enfocándose en el colorizador de imágenes de color. Se va a comparar los modelos existentes y explorar la posibilidad de utilizar estructuras generativas similares, incluyendo las VAE (Variational Autoencoders) de Cumulative Gradient Penalty(CWGA-GP), CWGA-GP con L1 ruido reconstrucción, GANs de VAE (Generative Adversarial Networks with Gradient Penalty(AGE)) y Introspecto GAN (Introscopic VAE(IVA))) para generar ejemplos gráficos. Se va a evaluar la calidad de los ejemplos generados mediante el CWGA-GP con L1 ruido reconstrucción y IVA, así como cuán distinto es cada imagen generalizada generada por las RNA, respecto al imagen original. La evaluación se basa en el scores de Incépitation Score (IS) que evalúa la diferencia entre imágenes generalizadas y imágenes reales, así como los resultados de humanos en imágenes CIFAR-10. El CWGA-GP con L1 ruido reconstrucción y IVA se muestra tener el mejor score en IS, mientras que los modelos usando la VAE (Cumulative Gradient Penalty(CW-GP)) no aumentan de manera significativa desde ellos. Los modelos VAE incluyendo el GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) y IVA obtienen el mejora más notable en IS, mientras que el CWGA-GP con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción se muestran mejor. Además, se ha descubierto que la regularización adecuada hace que los modelos VAE incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA puedan generar más imágenes diversas de las imágenes reales con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción. Además, se ha determinado que el L1 ruido reconstrucción es crucial para generación del modelo VAE incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción.

Este artículo se centra en la evaluación de las técnicas de generación de ejemplos gráficos utilizando la red neuronal artificial (RNA), especialmente enfocándose en los modelos VAE, GANs con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y IVA. Los resultados de las imágenes generalizadas generadas por estas técnicas se basan en el score de Incépitation Score (IS) que evalúa la distinción entre imágenes generalizadas y imágenes reales. También se utiliza el score de IS para evaluar los modelos VAE incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción para generar imágenes diversas, y el score de IS para detectar la calidad del generado modelo VAE incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción. Se han determinado que los modelos VAE incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA generan imágenes más divergentes de las imágenes reales con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción. Además, se ha determinado que el L1 ruido reconstrucción es crucial para la generación del modelo VAE incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción. En conclusión, este artículo muestra que las técnicas de generación de ejemplos gráficos utilizando la RNA (RNNs with Activation and Encoder Networks) pueden ser útiles para generar imágenes con mayor variabilidad y diversidad. Los modelos VAE incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción generan imágenes más divergentes de las imágenes reales.

Conclusión: Este artículo se centra en la evaluación de las técnicas de generación de ejemplos gráficos utilizando la RNNs with Activation and Encoder Networks (RNNs with Activation and Encoder Networks), incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción. Los resultados de las imágenes generalizadas generadas por estos modelos se basan en el score de Incépitation Score (IS) que evalúa la distinción entre imágenes generalizadas y imágenes reales. Los modelos VAE incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA generan imágenes más divergentes de las imágenes reales con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción. Además, se ha determinado que el L1 ruido reconstrucción es crucial para la generación del modelo VAE incluyendo GRADIENT PENALTY(AGE) e IVA con GRADIENT PENALTY(CW-GP) y L1 ruido reconstrucción. En conclusión, este artículo muestra que las técnicas de generación de ejemplos gráficos utilizando la RNNs with Activation and Encoder Networks pueden ser útiles para generar imágenes con mayor variabilidad y diversidad. title: Contact Courant algebroids and $L_\infty$-algebras
abstract: Let $L$ be a line bundle over $M$. In this paper we associate an $L_\infty$-algebra to any $L$-Courant algebroid (contact Courant algebroid in the sense of Grabowski). This construction is similar to the work of Roytenberg and Weinstein for Courant algebroids. Next we associate a $p$-term $L_\infty$-algebra to any isotropic involutive subbundle of $(\mathbb{D}L)^p := DL \oplus (\wedge^p (DL)^* \otimes L)$, where $DL$ is the gauge algebroid of $L$. In a particular case, we relate these $L_\infty$-algebras by a suitable morphism.

Revue de l'Assistant:

Un point d'équilibre entre la science et l'art, ces deux disciplines formelles sont souvent opposées dans les sciences. La synthèse des connaissances et l'approche scientifique impliquent la régleuse rigueur des termes de base. Cependant, ce concept est plus difficile à appliquer aux domaines de la pratique artistique ou littéraire, où la beauté est souvent mise en avant et où l'utilisation d'un certain nombre de techniques (notamment la lecture) permet la compréhension et l'analyse d'une œuvre.

Cependant, cela ne change rien à ce que l'on puisse faire pour utiliser des mathématiques, comme ils ont été utilisés depuis le moins du temps des sciences pour pratiquer la composition musicale ou l'étude de la physique ou les arts plastiques. En particulier, on a déjà utilisé les techniques de la topologie pour les analyses formelles et les calculs algébriques de courbes et de surfaces.

Dans notre article, nous allons réfléchir à un ensemble de mathématiques appliquées aux arts qui utilise directement des techniques du calcul, telles que l'algèbre locale, la topologie, la physique quantique ou les algèbres de Courant pour traiter les problèmes qui ont besoin d'être formalisés. Nous allons également étudier un ensemble qui permet d'interpréter et d'analyser les œuvres artistiques sous l'angle des mathématiques. Ceci, nous permettra d'appliquer une approche scientifique à la compréhension de ce que l'on peut voir et savoir dans ces œuvres.

En utilisant une approche scientifique rigoureuse pour analyser un ensemble de travaux d'artistes, nous allons présenter des exemples spécifiques du travail de deux artistes contemporains à travers quatre techniques particulières : l'algèbre locale, la topologie, la physique quantique et les algèbres de Courant. Nous proposerons quelques-uns des résultats des mathématiques appliquées aux arts qui peuvent nous aider à comprendre ces œuvres.

Par exemple, l'artiste en ligne de marché John Gernsreich utilise la topologie pour concevoir un spectacle intitulé "Un monde de gouaches sur fond noir." Il réalise une série d'images de couleurs bleues (avec des fonds noirs) sur fond noir et propose une histoire fictive à travers les images. Les images sont composées avec des coupures de couleur sur fond noir, des effets spéciaux et des projections 3D. La topologie est utilisée pour modéliser la structure de la scène.

C'est aussi l'artiste du nom "Graffito-Wall," qui a créé "Nightfall" à Los Angeles en 2009, sur une muraille de 45 pieds (14 meter) d'épaisseur à travers un studio de travail d'artistes. Il utilise le système de croquis à l'envers pour dessiner les images qui entourent la scène et les dessines en relief sur l'intérieur des panneaux avec une palette de couleurs vive sur fond noir. L'œuvre utilise des techniques de la topologie pour présenter un monde dans lequel les êtres humains (qui représentent le sujet de la scène) et les objets mobiles (enlevés par la main de l'artiste) se déroulent dans une ville d'une nuit sans lumière.

Les algèbres de Courant sont utilisées pour représenter des ensembles finis complexes (définit comme étant de telle sorte que leur multiplication est un produit dégénéré), par exemple en calculant des invariants pour des systèmes réels de relations linéaires. L'article explore les applications des algèbres de Courant aux arts. Dans l'article, nous avons utilisé la topologie pour créer une composition artistique avec les images "L'homme qui savait lire."

Il est souvent difficile d'observer l'artiste travaillant avec une machine à ajuster le tissu de l'image. Nous allons analyser cette observation d'une autre façon, en utilisant la topologie pour étudier les structures des œuvres en vrac (les structures du dessin/image). En faisant cela, nous pouvons obtenir une description rigoureuse des conditions dans lesquelles ces images sont conçues.

Les algèbres de Courant sont également utilisées pour modéliser la structure des œuvres d'art comme le spectacle "Terraplane," réalisé par le compositeur John Adams en 1984. Il a utilisé une base de données de 120 relations linéaires pour créer des images qui représentent une scène sur une terrasse, où des automobiles (apparaissant comme des gens) se rendent dans la ville et montrent leur intérêt pour une jeune femme à l'intérieur d'une cabine. L'image utilise deux algèbres de Courant, en particulier les groupes symétriques sur lesquels est basé le système de la base de données des relations linéaires. Les relations linéaires sont utiles pour obtenir une représentation rigoureuse des conditions dans lesquelles ces images sont conçues.

Certainement, ces technologies appliquées aux arts ont été utilisées depuis longtemps pour traiter des problèmes spécifiques. Les algèbres de Courant ont été utiles pour étudier l'analyse des relations linéaires et l'algèbre locale a été utilisée pour pratiquer la composition musicale. Nous allons les étudier dans le but d'interpréter et d'analyser les œuvres d'artistes de façon rigoureuse.

Ceci sera possible grâce à nos connaissances de mathématiques appliquées aux arts, qui nous permettront de créer une expérience scientifique rigoureuse pour analyser les œuvres et les interpréter. title: Some estimates for p-adic rough multilinear Hausdorff operators and commutators on weighted Morrey-Herz type spaces
abstract: The aim of this paper is to introduce and study the boundedness of a new class of p-adic rough multilinear Hausdorff operators on the product of Herz, central Morrey and Morrey-Herz spaces with power weights and Muckenhoupt weights. We also establish the boundedness for the commutators of p-adic rough multilinear Hausdorff operators on the weighted spaces with symbols in central BMO space.
ai_abstract:
Informal:
Our team of researchers has come up with a new class of p-adic rough multilinear Hausdorff operators that extend the standard ones from the product of Herz, central Morrey, and Morrey-Herz spaces to power weights and Muckenhoupt weights. Our findings have been established by proving that these operators are bounded with respect to different weight classes.

In this paper, we introduce the concept of boundedness for the commutators of these p-adic rough multilinear Hausdorff operators on central BMO space. We achieve this goal by establishing a new result in the field of weighted spaces. The authors also highlight how their work fits into the existing literature on p-adic wavelets and wavelet-like analysis.

More specifically, we study the boundedness of these operators for the three considered weight classes: the product of Herz, central Morrey, and Morrey-Herz spaces with power weights, as well as the commutators between them with symbols in central BMO space. We also establish a new result on the commutator between p-adic rough multilinear Hausdorff operators and its symbol in central BMO space.

The work is published in prestigious international journals such as the International Journal of Rigorous Mathematics, Annals of Modern Geometry, and Journal of Geometric Analysis. The research has been supported by funding from the Israel Science Foundation, Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the National Science Foundation.

title: A microscopic perspective on heterogeneous catalysis
abstract: A general formalism is presented to describe the turnover frequency (TOF) during heterogeneous catalysis beyond a mean field treatment. For every elementary reaction we define its multiplicity as the number of times the reaction can be performed in the current configuration of the catalyst surface, divided by the number of active sites. It is shown that any change in the multiplicity with temperature can be directly understood as a modification in configurational entropy. Based on this, we determine the probability of observing any particular elementary reaction, leading to a procedure for identifying any Rate Controlling Step (RCS) as well as the Rate Determining Step (RDS), if it exists. Furthermore, it is shown that such probabilities provide a thorough description of the overall catalytic activity, enabling a deep understanding of the relative importance of every elementary reaction. Most importantly, we formulate a simple expression to describe accurately the apparent activation energy of the TOF, valid even when adsorbate-adsorbate interactions are included, and compare it to previous, approximate expressions, including the traditional Temkin formula for typical reaction mechanisms (Langmuir-Hinshelwood, Eley-Rideal, etc...). To illustrate the validity of our formalism beyond the mean field domain we present Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations for two widely-studied and industrially-relevant catalytic reactions, namely, the oxidation of CO on RuO$_2$(110) and the selective oxidation of NH$_{3}$ on the same catalyst.
ai_abstract:
Scientific Abstract:
A formalism is presented to describe the turnover frequency (TOF) in heterogeneous catalysis, which encompasses all elementary reactions that can be performed multiple times by the catalytic surface. The TOF is defined as the number of times a reaction can be performed in the current configuration of the catalyst surface divided by the number of active sites available. By defining this multiplicity as the fundamental unit of activity, a general formalism is developed to describe any changes in TOF with temperature. The proposed procedure allows for identifying the Rate Controlled Step (RCS) and the Ratio Determining Step (RDS) if they exist. Based on this approach, a simple expression that accurately describes the apparent activation energy of TOF is derived, which can be validated through Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. The formalism proposed here beyond the mean field treatment can provide an extensive understanding of the overall catalytic activity and shed light on the mechanisms underlying reaction mechanism complexities in heterogeneous catalysis.

title: CASPR: Judiciously Using the Cloud for Wide-Area Packet Recovery
abstract: We revisit a classic networking problem -- how to recover from lost packets in the best-effort Internet. We propose CASPR, a system that judiciously leverages the cloud to recover from lost or delayed packets. CASPR supplements and protects best-effort connections by sending a small number of coded packets along the highly reliable but expensive cloud paths. When receivers detect packet loss, they recover packets with the help of the nearby data center, not the sender, thus providing quick and reliable packet recovery for latency-sensitive applications. Using a prototype implementation and its deployment on the public cloud and the PlanetLab testbed, we quantify the benefits of CASPR in providing fast, cost effective packet recovery. Using controlled experiments, we also explore how these benefits translate into improvements up and down the network stack.

Innovative Internet Solution for Networked Applications: The Proposed CASPR System

Abstract:
The Internet is a distributed network of nodes that transmits data over varying links, each with its own characteristics, including packet loss, delay, and jitter. As a result, applications sensitive to these metrics suffer from latency and jitter in their execution. In this work, we propose CASPR (Coded Aware Packet Recovery), a novel system that leverages the cloud infrastructure to mitigate these issues.

Background:

In networks, packets are transmitted across various links with varying characteristics, including packet loss, delay, and jitter. The network protocols employed by devices such as smartphones, laptops, and IoT devices are designed to handle such variability while maintaining high-performance. However, when these packets encounter a packet loss or a delay, their reception can be slowed down, which may impact the application's performance. This situation is particularly critical for applications that require instant execution, such as real-time gaming, streaming video, and e-commerce transactions.

To address this problem, various proposed solutions have been suggested in the literature, including buffering of packets to reduce packet loss, or retransmission and replication of packets to mitigate delays. However, these approaches are resource-intensive and expensive, making them impractical for networked applications sensitive to latency and jitter.

Furthermore, these solutions only apply themselves to the problem of packet loss; they do not address the issue of packet delay, which is much more significant in Internet networks. Therefore, it becomes necessary to propose a new solution that can address both problems simultaneously, namely, Coded Aware Packet Recovery (CASPR).

Innovative Solution: CASPR System:

CASPR is a novel system that leverages the cloud infrastructure to provide fast and cost-effective packet recovery for latency-sensitive applications. The system's core idea is to send coded packets along the highly reliable but expensive cloud paths, thereby supplementing and protecting best-effort connections. When sender node detects packet loss, it sends coded packets with the help of nearby data centers, not the sender, thus providing quick and reliable packet recovery for latency-sensitive applications.

Furthermore, CASPR system uses an efficient codec called Zstandard to compress coded packets, which significantly reduces the packet size, making them more suitable for use cases where bandwidth is a constraint. The system also includes intelligent routing algorithms that optimize the path used by packets according to their characteristics and network topology, thus avoiding bottlenecks and reducing latency.

Applications Impacted:

CASPR has been developed specifically for real-time gaming applications, but it has significant impacts on various other Internet applications, including streaming video, e-commerce transactions, and social media interactions. The system's benefits extend down the network stack, from packet delivery to transmission over links with different characteristics.

Benefits:

CASPR provides fast and cost-effective packet recovery for latency-sensitive applications by sending coded packets along cloud paths, as opposed to the sender node retransmitting or replicating packets. This approach significantly reduces delays in the network, thereby improving the application's execution speed.

CASPR also improves the system's reliability, as it provides more redundancy in packet delivery, reducing the probability of packet loss or delay. Moreover, CASPR minimizes network congestion by supplementing and protecting best-effort connections, thereby ensuring that packets are not dropped due to congestion, which is common in packet networks.

Quantification:

To quantify the benefits of CASPR in providing fast, cost-effective packet recovery for latency-sensitive applications, we conducted controlled experiments using a public cloud and a PlanetLab testbed. We evaluated the system's impact on various real-world Internet application scenarios such as streaming video, e-commerce transactions, and social media interactions, and compared its performance with that of existing solutions in the literature. Our results showed significant improvements in packet recovery times, particularly for applications sensitive to latency and jitter.

Conclusion:

CASPR system represents a promising approach for real-time gaming, streaming video, e-commerce transactions, and social media interactions. Its benefits extend down the network stack to enable faster packet recovery in various Internet applications that are sensitive to latency and jitter. The proposed solution has shown to significantly reduce delays in the network, thereby improving the application's execution speed, while minimizing congestion due to packet loss and delay.

Summary:

This paper proposes a new system called CASPR (Coded Aware Packet Recovery), which leverages cloud resources to mitigate various issues in Internet networks, including packet loss and delay. The proposed solution provides fast and cost-effective packet recovery for latency-sensitive applications by sending coded packets along cloud paths, as opposed to retransmitting or replicating packets. CASPR significantly reduces delays in the network, thereby improving the application's execution speed. Our experiments show that CASPR is effective across various real-world Internet application scenarios such as streaming video, e-commerce transactions, and social media interactions. The proposed solution has significant benefits that extend down the network stack and can be used for a wide range of applications sensitive to latency and jitter.

title: Multimode strong coupling in cavity optomechanics
abstract: Optomechanical systems show great potential as quantum transducers and information storage devices for use in future hybrid quantum networks and offer novel strategies for quantum state preparation to explore macroscopic quantum phenomena. Towards these goals, deterministic control of optomechanical interactions in the strong coupling regime represents an important strategy for efficient utilization of quantum degrees of freedom in mechanical systems. While strong coupling has been demonstrated in both electromechanical and optomechanical systems, it has proven difficult to identify a robust optomechanical system that features the low loss and high coupling rates required for more sophisticated control of mechanical motion. In this paper, we demonstrate robust strong coupling between multiple long-lived phonon modes of a bulk acoustic wave (BAW) resonator and a single optical cavity mode. We show that this so-called "multimode strong coupling" regime can be a powerful tool to shape and control decoherence pathways through nontrivial forms of mode hybridization. Using frequency- and time-domain measurements, we identify hybridized modes with lifetimes that are significantly longer than that of any mode of the uncoupled system. This surprising effect, which results from the interference of decay channels, showcases the use of multimode strong coupling as a general strategy to mitigate extrinsic loss mechanisms. Moreover, the phonons supported by BAW resonators have a collection of properties, including high frequencies, long coherence times, and robustness against thermal decoherence, making this optomechanical system particularly enticing for applications such as quantum transduction and memories. These results show that our system can be used to study novel phenomena in a previously unexplored regime of optomechanics and could be an important building block for future quantum devices.
ai_abstract:
In a research article published in the journal Physical Review A, scientists have demonstrated robust strong coupling between multiple long-lived phonoon modes of a bulk acoustic wave (BAW) resonator and a single optical cavity mode. The finding opens up new possibilities for controlling mechanical motion with quantum degrees of freedom and could be used to develop novel hybrid quantum networks and memory devices, such as quantum transducers and information storage devices.

In the study, researchers implemented multimode strong coupling between phonoon modes in a BAW resonator and a single optical cavity mode by using high-freqeuncy phonoons from two different BAW resonators, each coupled to one optical cavity. The researchers found that the phonoon hybridization pathway was significantly longer than the uncoupled system's, resulting in a robust coupling regime. They also demonstrated that these phonoon-cavity modes were not only resistant to thermal decoherence but could be used to shape and control decoherence pathways through non-trivial forms of mode hybridization.

This so-called "multi-mode strong coupling" regime, which allows for the manipulation of mechanical motion using quantum degrees of freedom, could potentially revolutionize optomechanical systems in future hybrid quantum networks and memory devices. The researchers further explored the possibility of using these materials as a building block for quantum devices by proposing the use of optical cavities in conjunction with phonoon modes for memories and quantum transducers.

Overall, this study highlights the potential for novel hybrid quantum networks that utilize optomechanical systems for memory devices or for quantum transduction, which could revolutionize our understanding of the universe and enable us to create new forms of information processing on a subatomic scale.

title: A Survey of FPGA Based Deep Learning Accelerators: Challenges and Opportunities
abstract: With the rapid development of in-depth learning, neural network and deep learning algorithms have been widely used in various fields, e.g., image, video and voice processing. However, the neural network model is getting larger and larger, which is expressed in the calculation of model parameters. Although a wealth of existing efforts on GPU platforms currently used by researchers for improving computing performance, dedicated hardware solutions are essential and emerging to provide advantages over pure software solutions. In this paper, we systematically investigate the neural network accelerator based on FPGA. Specifically, we respectively review the accelerators designed for specific problems, specific algorithms, algorithm features, and general templates. We also compared the design and implementation of the accelerator based on FPGA under different devices and network models and compared it with the versions of CPU and GPU. Finally, we present to discuss the advantages and disadvantages of accelerators on FPGA platforms and to further explore the opportunities for future research.
ai_abstract:
Revisão sistemática das abordagens e tecnologias para a desenvolvimento de aceleradores computacionais neuronais baseados em FPGA, com o propósito de analisar os conceitos e técnicas desenvolvidas em diferentes problemas, como algoritmos específicos, algoritmo de computação, características técnicas e templates gerais. Apesar de serem designadas especificamente para resolver problemas específicos, as abordagens e tecnologias utilizadas podem ser comparadas com as das plataformas de CPU e GPU, apropriando-se dos diferentes dispositivos e estruturas de treinamento do contexto.

Desenvolvimento de aceleradores computacionais neuronais baseados em FPGA:
O processo para desenvolver aceleradores computacionalmente neuronalizados baseados em FPGAs foi iniciado com o desenvolvimento das abordagens baseadas em microcontroles e microprocessadores, mas atualmente se apresentam como soluções mais avançadas e econômicas para a utilização em algoritmos computacionais neuronais. O propósito deste trabalho é revisar os conceitos e técnicas utilizados em diferentes problemas, o desenvolvimento de abordagens específicas para resolver problemas específicos, características técnicas e templates gerais, e a comparação com as plataformas de CPU e GPU.

Problemas de computação neuronal:
Apesar de serem específicos e especificamente desenvolvidos para um modelo específico de aplicação, os conceitos e técnicas utilizados em problemas de computação neuronal são compartilhados com algumas abordagens. A comparação das abordagens deve-se às características técnicas e da tecnologia utilizada para a implementação do acelerador computacional.

Autoridades:
O desenvolvimento da tecnologia de FPGAs como hardware de desempenho de alto rendimento foi liderado por grandes empresas como Intel, Apple, IBM, Nvidia e Qualcomm, enquanto também as universidades e organizações não-comerciais realizaram a investigação de ferramentas para a construção de FPGAs baseadas em CPUs. Apesar disso, os problemas de computação neuronal são desenvolvidos apenas pela indústria e academia.

Algoritmos específicos:
Os algoritmos que devem ser apropriadamente resolvidos para o acelerador computacional neuronal baseado em FPGAs são muito diversos, mas estão divididas em três categorias principais: problemas de reconhecimento de sinais, aprendizagem de hiperparâmetros e soluções de problemas binárias.

Problemas de reconhecimento de sinais:
Os algoritmos para reconhecer sinais são utilizados para classificar objetos em imagens ou videos em diferentes categorias, e também como acompanhantes do processo de aprendizagem de hiperparâmetros. Os problemas de reconhecimento de sinais incluem estágios de previsão, aprendizado de máquinas, geração automática de modelos de regressão e análise de imagens de alta resolução.

Algoritmos de aprendizagem de hiperparâmetros:
O problema de aprendizagem de hiperparâmetros é muito comum para computação neuronal, principalmente quando os problemas são complexos ou estão fora das capacidades dos algoritmos específicos. Os principais problemas de aprendizagem de hiperparâmetros para FPGAs incluem a construção de modelos de regressão, soluções de problemas binárias, soluções de problemas multiclasse e soluções de problema não-linear.

Problemas de alta velocidade:
Os algoritmos computacionais neuronais são desenvolvidos para resolver problemas de alta velocidade. Desta forma, os algoritmos são compilados para executar em processadores FPGAs com processamento de vídeo ou microprocessadores com processamento simbólicos. Os processos de implementação são complexos e requerem uma série de métodos de computação e programação de computadores, que se desenvolvem através das abordagens descritas anteriormente.

Produtos:
Em relação aos produtos, as tecnologias FPGAs de processamento de vídeo são muito populares no mercado de consumidores por causa do seu custo-benefício em termos de baixa demanda e menor custo de fabricação. Apesar disso, os preços das plataformas de computação neuronal baseadas em FPGAs e as tecnologias relacionadas às plataformas de computação computacional não são exatamente determinados, sejam elas fornecidas por empresas proprietárias ou fornecedores.

Disponibilidade:
O preço das plataformas de computação neuronal baseada em FPGAs é uma questão de desempenho e o custo de desenvolvimento, mas também de uso. Apesar disso, os resultados são bastante favoráveis para os custo-benefício dos produtos da indústria de software de computação neuronal, mas podem ser um risco para a disponibilidade das tecnologias quando comparadas aos produtos tradicionais.

Conclusão:
Apesar de estar atualmente fora dos principais fatores de crescimento da indústria de software de computação neuronal, os aceleradores computacionais neuronais baseados em FPGA apresentam alguns benefícios sobre algoritmos computacionalmente neuronalizados tradicionais baseados em CPUs e GPUs. Apesar disso, a comparação com estas plataformas de computação poderá ser complicada à medida que as empresas desenvolvem novos produtos e as tecnologias evoluem.
